Hard gate: NO release actions — no version bump, tag, publish, deploy, or merge to main. Hunter gates all of that. Pushing the integration branch to run CI is always fine. Keep the branch green; verify everything yourself, never trust prior claims (a false "suite green" hid a stack overflow this cycle).

Mission

Close out ALL 128 open issues (gh issue list --state open) and process all 13 open PRs. Tracker: #5573. Priority order: P0 safety/money (#5567 fleet cost ceiling, #5568 sandbox read deny-list, #5569 hard-link write escape, #5543→PR#5584 child approval receipts, #5552 doctor --fix) → bugs (#5597, #5595, #5583, #5582, #5578, #5577, #5572, #5562, #5529, #5528, #5522, #5290, #5601, #5605, #5564) → UX (#5589, #5556, #5555, #5551, #5550, #5549, #5479, #5271, #5268) → neutrality/structure epics (#5588, #5586, #5580, #5587, #5575, #5316, #5443, #5103, #5092-5094, #5249, #5362, #5226) → plugin UX #5579, #5548, #5519, #5482. PRs: exact dispositions

- Take now (merge --no-ff, preserve authorship, verify full suite, changelog receipts): #5592 (lifecycle outbox, +4.4k, Hunter-approved, expects conflicts in engine dispatch vs #5606 — take #5606's code placed into the new module layout) and #5593 (/relaunch, Hunter-approved).
- #5606 (Hunter's relay, 19.4k): take once he adds a Closes #N line to the PR body (link gate). Diagnosis already posted on the PR.

- Dependabot PRs land only with green full CI.

In flight RIGHT NOW (uncommitted in working tree — finish first)

The agy/Antigravity sign-in fix. Root cause verified against the real state.vscdb: the token is a base64 protobuf envelope under antigravityUnifiedStateSync.oauthToken (field1 ya29. access, field2 "Bearer", field3 1// refresh, field4 expiry epoch) plus a LIVE credential in antigravityAuthStatus JSON apiKey. Implementation exists: crates/tui/src/agy_credentials/envelope.rs (new; parses both shapes, auth-status wins, expired envelope → absent, refresh token parsed-past-and-dropped per read-only contract) + reworked agy_credentials.rs (queries both rows, resolve_external_credential precedence). Rules (violations have broken this repo before)

Commit only files you changed; file-scoped rustfmt --check; clippy --tests; full cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked (~11.2k tests, ~2min) green between commits. Trailer: Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> (or another allowed identity from scripts/check-coauthor-trailers.py). Any feat: referencing #N needs a #N CHANGELOG receipt (gate: scripts/release/check-feature-release-notes.sh); after ANY root CHANGELOG edit run scripts/sync-changelog.sh or Version-drift fails. Invariants (AGENTS.md): one turn loop (Engine::run_turn, guard test in crates/core/tests/single_turn_loop.rs); BASE_PROMPT sole in crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs; KV-cache prefix contract docs/CACHE.md; modules repeatedly misidentified as dead are listed in AGENTS.md — verify consumers before deleting. Windows CI legs have a 1h30m cap — a "cancelled" windows leg = timeout, just re-push. Known flake #5605 (passes isolated). Small coherent fixes commit directly; one PR per logical workstream.

Done this cycle (do NOT redo)

9 mechanical #5586 extractions (lib.rs 18.7k→13.1k, config.rs→10.2k, client.rs→10.6k, runtime_threads.rs→8.3k: client/{wire,redaction,wire_dialect}.rs, config/{merge,credentials}.rs, cli_args.rs, doctor_cli.rs, exec_agent.rs, runtime_threads/{agent_mail,store}.rs), #5585 fix (parse_config_toml_str 16MiB thread in codewhale-config + test restructure), PRs #5602/#5603/#5604 taken, docs/AUTOMATION.md + README/GUIDE links (d070d510c), provider-registry lint follows module trees (079ebc512), wire_config_prefers_anthropic dedup, #5600/#5605 filed, #5573 reconciled. This includes: architectural decisions, debugging intricate issues, writing critical business logic, refactoring complex systems, security audits, performance optimization, or any situation where getting it right the first time is essential. This is your 'bring in the expert' agent for tasks that justify the higher cost and slower speed of Opus-level reasoning.

Examples:

<example>
Context: User needs to redesign the authentication system architecture.
user: "We need to migrate from session-based auth to JWT tokens while maintaining backward compatibility. Can you help design this?"
assistant: "This is a critical architectural decision that requires careful analysis. Let me use the opus-strategist agent to develop a comprehensive migration strategy."
<commentary>
Since this involves security-critical architecture with backward compatibility requirements, use the opus-strategist agent to ensure thorough analysis of edge cases, security implications, and migration risks.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>

user: "We have a race condition that only appears in production under load. The workspace sometimes shows stale data even after the sandbox reports success."
assistant: "This sounds like a subtle concurrency issue. I'll engage the opus-strategist agent to systematically analyze the possible race conditions in the E2B sandbox and workspace synchronization flow."
<commentary>
Complex race conditions require methodical reasoning about state, timing, and edge cases. The opus-strategist agent excels at this type of deep analysis.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>

user: "Implement the Stripe usage metering for workspace_seconds. This needs to be bulletproof - we can't overbill or underbill customers."
assistant: "Billing accuracy is critical for trust and compliance. I'll use the opus-strategist agent to implement this with comprehensive error handling, idempotency, and audit trails."
<commentary>
Money-related features require exceptional care. The opus-strategist agent will consider edge cases like network failures, duplicate events, and reconciliation.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to refactor a core system component.
user: "The agent loop is getting unwieldy. Help me refactor it to be more maintainable without breaking any existing functionality."
assistant: "Refactoring core infrastructure requires understanding all the interdependencies. Let me bring in the opus-strategist agent to analyze the current implementation and design a safe refactoring approach."
<commentary>
Core system refactoring benefits from the opus-strategist's ability to hold complex systems in context and identify subtle breaking changes.
</commentary>

user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"

</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"

user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"

## claude.ai Context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

# Codewhale agent guidance

Keep this file durable. Derive changing release, provider, branch, and flake
state from the repository, tests, CI, and current issue tracker rather than from
instructions or memory. The nearest scoped `AGENTS.md` adds path-specific rules.

## Working rules

- Inspect status and existing consumers before editing. Preserve unrelated,
  dirty, and untracked work.
- Prefer the simplest implementation that preserves observable contracts. A
  rewrite is acceptable when justified by product intent and observed behavior,
  not as a shortcut around understanding existing code.
- Search for behavior and symbols before reviving work from an old branch. If a
  lane is obsolete, preserve its intent and evidence rather than merging stale
  code mechanically.
- A small coherent change may be committed directly to `main` when that checkout
  is current, clean, and owns the affected files. A worktree remains the right
  safety boundary for conflicting, dirty, stale, or independent work. Local
  commit permission never implies push, merge, tag, release, or deploy permission.
- When the task is local-only, stay fully offline: no browsing, GitHub or remote
  Git operations, downloads, dependency installation, provider calls, or
  source/diff transmission. Record the missing external receipt and keep working
  locally.
- Public name is **Codewhale**. Compatibility identifiers such as `CodeWhale`,
  `codew`, protocol names, and storage keys change only through an explicit
  migration.
- Keep providers and models first-class and provider-neutral.
- Never rewrite published history, retag a release, force-push a shared ref, or
  publish without explicit authorization. Preserve human contributor credit.

## Current contracts

- The model-facing subagent tool is `agent`. Do not revive removed
  `agent_open`/`agent_eval`/`agent_close`/`delegate_to_agent` surfaces or parallel
  lifecycle/tag systems.
- `BASE_PROMPT` in `crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs` is the sole base prompt.
- There is exactly one turn loop: `Engine::run_turn` in
  `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs`. Note that `crates/tui/src/core/`
  is a module inside the TUI crate — it is not `crates/core`, which owns
  request construction, bounded fragments, and thread/session types and
  runs no turns. Do not add a second loop beside the one that exists; a
  guard test (`crates/core/tests/single_turn_loop.rs`) fails if you do.
- The system prompt + tool catalog are a session-pinned KV-cache prefix
  (`docs/CACHE.md`). Any new session-context contributor must state its
  KV-cache effect: frozen prefix vs. append-only history. Never splice a
  volatile fact into the prefix; append it as a user-role message.
- These active modules are repeatedly misidentified as dead; verify consumers
  before removal: `tui/src/context_budget.rs`, `tui/src/model_registry.rs`,
  `tui/src/prompt_zones.rs`, `tui/src/tools/remember.rs`, and
  `config/src/route/`. Native memory lives in `tui/src/native_memory.rs`;
  `tools/remember.rs` is its capture path.
- Environment-specific behavior belongs in `docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md`, not here.

## Code, migrations, and evidence

- Product intent and observed runtime behavior outrank a test's preferred
  implementation shape. Fix the product; do not contort production code to
  preserve a brittle assertion.
- Tests are selective evidence, not the specification. Do not add tests by
  default. Add or retain one when it cheaply protects a high-risk behavior such
  as safety, data integrity, protocol compatibility, or a reproduced regression.
- Rewrite or remove tests that duplicate coverage, freeze internals, overspecify
  copy or layout, preserve obsolete behavior, or cost more than the risk they
  cover. Never weaken real safety or data-integrity behavior merely to make a
  gate pass.
- Prefer focused compilation, a relevant existing check, and direct product or
  manual evidence. Run a broad suite only when the change creates a genuine
  cross-cutting or release risk. Do not repeatedly rerun an unchanged suite.
- Declared migrations are one-way. Once the repository adopts a replacement
  architecture or shared spine, new work uses it and touched legacy code moves
  toward it. Do not add another legacy call site for convenience. Keep a
  compatibility path only for an actual external contract, and label that
  boundary explicitly.

Useful commands, selected according to risk rather than run ritualistically:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p codewhale-config -p codewhale-protocol
cargo test --workspace
cargo build --release -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-tui
```

`cargo nextest run` (config in `.config/nextest.toml`) is the fast way to
run an intentionally selected suite; `cargo test --no-run` can answer a compile
question without spending time executing unrelated cases, and `cargo test --doc`
covers doc examples when those examples changed.
`scripts/dev-test.sh <area>` maps a code area to its fastest `-p` invocation
and applies the portable isolated build-dir topology for new worktrees
(`scripts/dev-cache.sh`, `scripts/dev-cargo.sh`). See
`docs/BUILD_PERFORMANCE.md`.

Report commands actually run and distinguish source, local tests, packaged
artifacts, CI, and public release state. Describe the evidence actually needed
for the claim; a test count is not a proxy for product quality.

Community reports, PRs, logs, and reviews are evidence. Canonical human
identities come from `.github/AUTHOR_MAP`; `Co-authored-by` credit is for
humans and for recognized agent contributors (the exact identities listed in
`AGENT_CONTRIBUTOR_IDENTITIES` in `scripts/check-coauthor-trailers.py`, such as
`Codewhale Agent`); unknown bot/tool trailers are still rejected.
Leave unrelated work intact and keep new enforcement dry-run unless explicitly
approved.

Edition 2024 requires explicit unsafe { } blocks with // SAFETY: comments inside unsafe fn.

  Context / scope decision (already made, do not re-litigate):
  Computer use has three future environments: workspace (agent's own machine, the Devin-shaped product), host (the user's real desktop), device (Android/HarmonyOS). The user decided to build host-only first, and the workspace lane comes later built on the same primitives. The north-star doc is already written at docs/design/COMPUTER_USE_WORKSPACE.md — don't rewrite it, just keep new work compatible. The phase-2 design is docs/design/COMPUTER_USE_BACKGROUND.md (element-level AX control, background input via AXPress/CGEventPostToPid, per-app consent). The phase-1 crate (crates/computer-use) is pixel-based foreground control and is complete; your job is phase 2 on top of it.

  Architecture already in place (all compiles or nearly so):

  1. src/consent.rs (NEW, done): per-app consent. Policy { allow, deny, host_terminal, host_terminal_pid }, Verdict { Allowed, NeedsApproval, Denied, Excluded }, hard exclusions (SecurityAgent, loginwindow, System Settings, Codewhale itself, host terminal). needs_approval_error() returns a structured needs_app_approval: message naming the app and the exact [apps] allow = [...] line to add. Has tests.

  2. src/elements.rs (NEW, done): ElementDriver trait (apps, app_state, act, raise, caps), types AppInfo, WindowInfo, AppState, ElementNode, ElementAction enum (Press/Click/SetValue/Type/Key/Menu/Scroll/SelectText/Drag), ActionReceipt { text, verified, moved }, StateMode { Full, Image, Ax }, render_nodes(). Has tests.

  3. src/driver.rs (MODIFIED, done): added fn element(&mut self) -> Option<&mut dyn ElementDriver> with default None to the Driver trait.

  5. src/session.rs (MODIFIED, done): new tools computer_apps, computer_app_state, computer_element, computer_raise in the catalog; app argument added to computer_click/scroll/type/key/drag routed via routed_app_action(); consent gate gate_app(); app resolution resolve_app(); AppSnapshot cache keyed by app label. All wired into call() dispatch.

  6. src/drivers/mock.rs (MODIFIED, done): MockDriver implements ElementDriver when element_enabled.

  7. src/drivers/macos.rs (MODIFIED, done): MacDriver gained element_snapshot: Option<MacElementSnapshot> field, element() returns Some(self), pub(crate) helpers backing_scale(), accessibility_granted(), need_accessibility(), and keycode()/modifier_flags() made pub(crate). Added cf_boolean_true() helper.

  8. src/drivers/mod.rs (MODIFIED): registers #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] pub mod macos_ax;.

  9. src/lib.rs (MODIFIED): registers consent + elements modules; calls macos_ax::detect_host_terminal() at startup to populate cfg.apps.host_terminal_pid.

  THE BLOCKER / what to finish first:

  src/drivers/macos_ax.rs — I DELETED it after a bad first draft. You must rewrite it from scratch. It is the macOS AX element backend. Requirements:

  - FFI bindings to CoreFoundation (CFString/CFArray/CFDicationServices (AXUIElement,CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo, CGWindowListCreateImage, CGEventPostToPid), CoreGraphics (CGEventCreate, CGImage*, CGRectMakeWithDictionaryRepresentation), and libproc (proc_pidpath).
  - Implement ElementDriver for MacDriver (methods: appsaps).
  - apps(): use CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo to build the running-app list; group windows by owner pid; only layer==0 windows; get bundle ids by reading the .app's Info.plist CFBundleIdentifier (parse from the plist XML, handle $(PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER) as None).
  - app_state(): match the AX window by title (fallback: position), walk the AX tree with AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue(kAXChildrenAttribute) capped at depth ~24 / ~1500 nodes, capture the window image with CGWindowListCreateImage(kCGWindowListOptionIncludingWindow, window_id), convert BGRA→RGBA, downscale to opts.max_edge, convert node
  frames from window-local points to image pixels using uded by checking if any layer-0 window in front of it
  fully covers it. Store a MacElementSnapshot (retained geometry) so index-based actions work later.
  - act(): take the snapshot, dispatch on ElementAction. Press → AXPress, fallback background click at node center via CGEventPostToPid (window-local points, NOT global). SetValue → AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(kAXValueAttribute) + read-back for verified, fallback
  focus+select-all+type for Electron. Type/Key → CGEvent Menu → AXShowMenu. Scroll →CGEventCreateScrollWheelEvent2 posted to pid, read scroll bar AXValue before/after for moved. SelectText → AXValueCreate with CFRange → kAXSelectedTextRangeAttribute. Drag → mouse down/dragged/up posted to pid.
  - raise() → osascript set frontmost of (first process whose unix id is PID) to true.
  - detect_host_terminal() -> Option<(u32, String)>: walk the parent-pid chain with /bin/ps -o ppid=,comm= -p PID skipping shells/codewhale itself.
  - Tests: parse_bundle_identifier (plist XML), bgra_to_ith stride), bundle_id_from_executable_path.

  Key correctness notes:
  - CGEventPostToPid coordinates are window-local points (origin at the window's top-left), not global screen points. Do not add the window origin.
  - All AXUIElement refs retained in the snapshot must be CFReleased in Drop for MacElementSnapshot.
  - encode_png takes &RgbImage not &RgbaImage — convert before encoding, or add an RGBA encode path.
  - warnings = "deny" means no unused imports, no unused variables.

  After macos_ax.rs compiles and tests pass:

  1. Add ElementDriver to the Windows driver (src/drivers/windows.rs) — reads only for now: apps() via EnumWindows, app_state() with window_image only (no AX tree on Windows yet, return empty nodes with a note), act() returns DriverError::Unsupported for everything. caps() = { tree: false, window_image: true, background_actions: false, note: "Windows: window capture only; use foreground pixel tools for actions" }.

  2. Add ElementDriver to Android (src/drivers/android.rs) and HarmonyOS (src/drivers/harmony.rs): map Press → tap at node center via existing input tap, SetValue → input text, apps() → running packages, app_state() → existing ui_tree() nodes converted to ElementNode with a synthetic full-screen image. caps() = { tree: true, window_image: false, background_actions: false }.

  3. Update the bundle files in crates/computer-use/bundle/:
  - skills/computer-use/SKILL.md: add the background/element workflow (computer_apps → computer_app_state → computer_element by index, app arg on click/type/key/scroll/drag, consent gate, needs_app_approval handling).
  - plugin.json: bump version to 0.2.0.
  - README.md: note the new tools.

  4. Update docs/COMPUTER_USE.md: add a "Background / element control" section covering the new tools, the consent model, and the macOS permission requirements.

  5. Update src/setup.rs: write an initial [apps] section to computer-use.toml during setup (with a comment explaining the allow/deny lists), and detect the host terminal to add it to the exclusion list in the printed next-steps.

  Verification gates (must all pass before you're done):
  - cargo test -p codewhale-computer-use — all tests gre
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy -p codewhale-computer-use --all-targets -- -D warnings
  - cargo build --release -p codewhale-computer-use
  - The TUI bundle validation test: cargo test -p codewhale-tui shipped_computer_use_bundle — the bundle files you update must match what the TUI expects (it validates plugin.json structure, skill count, MCP server command, etc.)
  - OHOS dependency guard: bash scripts/ohos/*.sh or whatever the OHOS guard script is (check scripts/ohos/)

  What NOT to do:
  - Do not commit to main. Work on the existing branch o
  - Do not touch crates/tui/src/ except if the bundle validation test fails and requires a TUI-side fix.
  - Do not implement the workspace/container lane — that's phase 3, documented in COMPUTER_USE_WORKSPACE.md.
  - Do not add nightly features.
  - Do not weaken any existing safety or data-integrity behavior to make a gate pass.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(credentials): parse the agy state.vscdb token envelope for sign-in

Antigravity 1.1.13 no longer stores a bare token under
`antigravityUnifiedStateSync.oauthToken`. The value is a base64 protobuf
envelope (marker message + inner base64 blob carrying the access token,
"Bearer", a refresh token, and an expiry), so the old bare-string parser
handed the whole blob back as if it were a credential and sign-in failed.

Parse both shapes the store actually carries. `antigravityAuthStatus` is
the row the app keeps current, so its JSON `apiKey` wins; the envelope is
the fallback and is honored only while its recorded expiry is still in
the future. An expired envelope reads as absent, not as an error — the
honest outcome is "sign in to Antigravity again", which is the same
read-only, never-refresh contract this module has always stated. Legacy
bare-string and JSON values still import through the original parser.

The refresh token is parsed past and dropped rather than retained: this
import never refreshes the external store, so holding the value would be
secret material kept for no purpose. No token material is logged, and
the tests build synthetic envelopes rather than using real fixtures.

Evidence:
  cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib agy_credentials
    -> 16 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
    -> 11188 passed; 0 failed; 13 ignored (135.81s)
  cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --lib --tests -> clean
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check (both files) -> clean

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

=== IMAGE PLACEHOLDER ===
SUMMARY:
 The composer has exactly one display-vs-buffer hook today — `App::composer_display_input()`/`composer_display_cursor()` (crates/tui/src/tui/app/composer.rs:574,578) — but it is a whole-buffer swap for history search, returns `&str`, and is bypassed by the mouse hit-testing path (crates/tui/src/tui/mouse_ui.rs:174,239 read raw `app.input`), so it is not a usable hook for a partial, per-line transform without adding an index map. Design A (render-only `[Image #N]`) is feasible but forces a display↔buffer char-index mapping through the composer's most fragile math: cursor row/col (widgets/mod.rs:4062, which documents a prior caret-desync regression), selection ranges (widgets/mod.rs:1504), mouse mapping, and atomic cursor motion. Design B (shorten the stored line) touches one producer (app.rs:5865), one parser (file_mention.rs:757), and ~18 tests — much lower risk — but the literal DOES live in persisted cross-version state (saved sessions re-read by backtrack, offline_queue.json, composer_history.txt, composer_stash.jsonl), and one consumer of the parser is the Runtime-Chat path-redaction guard, so the parser must keep accepting the legacy form rather than being renamed. Note also that design B as described still leaves the full path in the line, so it does not actually deliver Claude Code's compact token.

RECOMMENDATION:
 RECOMMENDATION: Design B is lower risk by a wide margin — but be clear with the user that **B as specified does not achieve the stated goal**. Dropping the description turns `[Attached image: 1920x1440 PNG (2.3MB) at /Users/x/Library/.../Screenshot 2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]` into `[Image #1: /Users/x/Library/.../Screenshot 2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]`. That removes ~28 characters, and the path — normally the longest part — is still there. Claude Code's compact `[Image #1]` is only reachable by hiding the path, i.e. design A or a side table.

RISK ORDER, concretely:
- B (rename + drop description): ~10 production lines + doc/test churn, zero index-space math. Lowest risk.
- A (render-only): no persistence risk at all, but it forces a display↔buffer index map through the single most fragile code in the composer.
- Side table (buffer holds `[Image #1]`, path in a map): lowest visual noise, highest risk — it is exactly what image_attach.rs:8 was written to refuse, and it breaks the four durability paths enumerated in the findings (backtrack, offline queue, stash, history recall).

MINIMAL PLAN FOR B:
1. `crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs:5865` `media_attachment_reference` — add an `index: usize` parameter; emit `format!("[Image #{n}: {}]", path.display())` for `kind == "image"`, and `[Video #{n}: {path}]` (or keep `[Attached {kind}: {path}]`) for other kinds. Drop the `description` argument's use in the emitted text; keep the description for the status toast at composer.rs:868.
2. `crates/tui/src/tui/app/composer.rs:696` `insert_media_attachment` — compute `n = self.composer_attachment_count() + 1` before building the reference. (Correct only when appending at the end; see numbering below.)
3. `crates/tui/src/tui/file_mention.rs:757` `media_attachment_references` — make the parser accept BOTH forms. Keep the existing `strip_prefix("[Attached ")` branch untouched, add a branch that matches `[Image` / `[Video` optionally followed by ` #<digits>`, then `: `, then the path. Keep the ` at ` rsplit only on the legacy branch so a path containing " at " is safe in the new format (and note that `stable_attachment_name`, line 833, can then stop mangling names for new attachments — leave it, it is harmless).
4. Update the doc comments that name the format: image_attach.rs:8 and :427, core/engine.rs:3379, session_peek.rs:556, runtime_handoff.rs:516, file_mention.rs:61 and :833. Update docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2495-2513 ("Local Media Attachments").
5. Tests that assert the literal and must be updated (all currently green on the old shape): crates/tui/src/tui/app/tests.rs:4755, 4759, 4770, 4809; crates/tui/src/commands/contract.rs:1045, 1123; crates/tui/src/tui/file_mention.rs:1667, 1900, 1910, 2348; crates/tui/src/image_attach/tests.rs:230, 266, 312, 392, 410, 422; crates/tui/src/core/engine/tests.rs:6048; crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs:6733. ADD one test that the *legacy* `[Attached image: 8x4 PNG at /tmp/p.png]` line still parses — that is the migration guard.

NUMBERING (design B): numbering is positional over `media_attachment_references(&self.input)` order, and the number lives in the buffer, so it goes stale the moment the buffer is edited. Delete #1 of 3 and the remaining lines still read `#2` and `#3`. Two honest options: (a) accept gaps — the parser ignores the digits entirely, so correctness is unaffected and only the labels look odd; (b) add a `renumber_attachments(&mut self)` pass called at the end of `insert_media_attachment` (composer.rs:696) and `remove_selected_composer_attachment` (composer.rs:766). (b) is doable — both functions already do `replace_range` with cursor fixup — but it makes every attachment mutation rewrite unrelated bytes of the buffer, which perturbs `cursor_position`, `selection_anchor`, and the undo/`clear_undo_buffer` snapshot. It also cannot fix hand-editing (the user deleting a line with Backspace never calls either function). I would ship (a) plus renumber-on-insert-only, and note that a user who manually deletes a line sees a gap.

IF YOU ACTUALLY WANT `[Image #1]` (design A), the bounded shape is: build one `ComposerDisplay { text: String, display_to_buffer: Vec<usize>, buffer_to_display: Vec<usize> }` once per frame from `app.input`, collapsing each whole attachment *line* to a single token, and route EVERY one of these through it — widgets/mod.rs:1281-1282, the `selection_range()` comparison at 1504, `cursor_pos` at 1826-1827, frame.rs:1093-1094 and 1124, mouse_ui.rs:174 and 239. Then make the token atomic for editing: `move_cursor_left`/`move_cursor_right` (composer.rs:1127/1133) and the backspace/delete path must jump the whole line, otherwise the caret appears frozen for ~60 keypresses while crossing one attachment. That is roughly 8 call sites plus cursor-motion work, all in the code whose own comments record a caret-desync regression (widgets/mod.rs:4062-4069) and a selection-index bug (#3909, widgets/mod.rs:1505).

RISKS:
 MIGRATION — SAY THIS LOUDLY: the `[Attached ` literal DOES live in persisted, cross-version state, in four places, and three of them are re-parsed after a restart.

1. Saved sessions. The submitted user text is stored verbatim as a `ContentBlock::Text` in the session JSON (core/engine.rs:3399-3402). Resume alone is safe — the `ImageUrl` blocks were expanded at send time and round-trip with the session — BUT `apply_backtrack` (ui/apply.rs:2444, `app.input = user_text` at 2477) puts that stored text back into the composer. A 0.9.11 session resumed and rewound under a rename-only parser shows zero attachment rows and, on resend, silently drops the image to plain text. Existing test: crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs:6731 `backtrack_prefill_rehydrates_attachment_rows`.
2. `sessions/checkpoints/offline_queue.json` (session_manager.rs:1375, restored at ui/event_loop.rs:389). Queued/draft text written by 0.9.11 is re-parsed on next launch and resent.
3. `~/.codewhale/composer_history.txt` (composer_history.rs:202) — raw lines, so old attachment lines sit there individually and come back on Up-arrow.
4. `~/.codewhale/composer_stash.jsonl` (composer_stash.rs) — parked drafts, popped verbatim.

Mitigation is cheap and one-way-safe: make the parser at file_mention.rs:757 accept both prefixes forever and only change the producer. That is additive, needs no version gate, and keeps every stored artifact working. Do NOT ship a rename that removes the legacy branch.

NOT a contract surface: ACP (acp_server.rs touches only `strip_images_when_unsupported`, never the text token), session_peek.rs:556 and runtime_handoff.rs:516 (doc comments only — neither parses the literal), web/, and the locale files.

SECURITY: `sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments` (core/engine.rs:130) is the Runtime-Chat isolation guard — it redacts attachment lines so a managed-chat host never sees a local path. It shares the one parser. A parser that stops recognizing a form that can still reach the composer (any of the four stores above) turns that guarantee off silently: the raw local path is sent to the managed provider. This is the single strongest argument for "add a branch, never replace one".

TESTS ASSERTING CURRENT BEHAVIOR (18 sites, listed in the plan above). The ones that are genuinely load-bearing rather than copy-freezing: image_attach/tests.rs:392 and :410 (missing-file notice, multi-attachment order), commands/contract.rs:1045/1123 (the `/attach` → composer contract for image and video), ui/tests.rs:6731 (backtrack rehydration), file_mention.rs:1899 (`media_attachment_references_include_removable_line_ranges` — the byte ranges the delete path depends on). Per AGENTS.md the rest are candidates for rewrite rather than mechanical string updates.

RISK IF DESIGN A IS CHOSEN INSTEAD: no persistence risk whatsoever, but the failure modes are user-visible and hard to test — caret drifting off the drawn text (widgets/mod.rs:4062 documents the last time that happened), selection highlight painting the wrong columns (widgets/mod.rs:1504-1512), mouse clicks landing at the wrong char index (mouse_ui.rs:174 reads the raw buffer while frame.rs:1093 published padding/scroll from the display text), and arrow keys appearing to stall inside a collapsed token. Wrap math itself is fine as long as the transform is applied before `wrap_input_lines_internal`, since that function only assumes lines concatenate back to whatever string it was handed.

That is roughly 8 call sites plus cursor-motion work, all in the code whose own comments record a caret-desync regression (widgets/mod.rs:4062-4069) and a selection-index bug (#3909, widgets/mod.rs:1505).

1. Saved sessions. The submitted user text is stored verbatim as a `ContentBlock::Text` in the session JSON (core/engine.rs:3399-3402). Resume alone is safe — the `ImageUrl` blocks were expanded at send time and round-trip with the session — BUT `apply_backtrack` (ui/apply.rs:2444, `app.input = user_text` at 2477) puts that stored text back into the composer. A 0.9.11 session resumed and rewound under a rename-only parser shows zero attachment rows and, on resend, silently drops the image to plain text. Existing test: crates/tui/src/tui/ui/tests.rs:6731 `backtrack_prefill_rehydrates_attachment_rows`.
2. `sessions/checkpoints/offline_queue.json` (session_manager.rs:1375, restored at ui/event_loop.rs:389). Queued/draft text written by 0.9.11 is re-parsed on next launch and resent.
3. `~/.codewhale/composer_history.txt` (composer_history.rs:202) — raw lines, so old attachment lines sit there individually and come back on Up-arrow.
4. `~/.codewhale/composer_stash.jsonl` (composer_stash.rs) — parked drafts, popped verbatim.

Mitigation is cheap and one-way-safe: make the parser at file_mention.rs:757 accept both prefixes forever and only change the producer. That is additive, needs no version gate, and keeps every stored artifact working. Do NOT ship a rename that removes the legacy branch.

NOT a contract surface: ACP (acp_server.rs touches only `strip_images_when_unsupported`, never the text token), session_peek.rs:556 and runtime_handoff.rs:516 (doc comments only — neither parses the literal), web/, and the locale files.

SECURITY: `sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments` (core/engine.rs:130) is the Runtime-Chat isolation guard — it redacts attachment lines so a managed-chat host never sees a local path. It shares the one parser. A parser that stops recognizing a form that can still reach the composer (any of the four stores above) turns that guarantee off silently: the raw local path is sent to the managed provider. This is the single strongest argument for "add a branch, never replace one".

TESTS ASSERTING CURRENT BEHAVIOR (18 sites, listed in the plan above). The ones that are genuinely load-bearing rather than copy-freezing: image_attach/tests.rs:392 and :410 (missing-file notice, multi-attachment order), commands/contract.rs:1045/1123 (the `/attach` → composer contract for image and video), ui/tests.rs:6731 (backtrack rehydration), file_mention.rs:1899 (`media_attachment_references_include_removable_line_ranges` — the byte ranges the delete path depends on). Per AGENTS.md the rest are candidates for rewrite rather than mechanical string updates.

RISK IF DESIGN A IS CHOSEN INSTEAD: no persistence risk whatsoever, but the failure modes are user-visible and hard to test — caret drifting off the drawn text (widgets/mod.rs:4062 documents the last time that happened), selection highlight painting the wrong columns (widgets/mod.rs:1504-1512), mouse clicks landing at the wrong char index (mouse_ui.rs:174 reads the raw buffer while frame.rs:1093 published padding/scroll from the display text), and arrow keys appearing to stall inside a collapsed token. Wrap math itself is fine as long as the transform is applied before `wrap_input_lines_internal`, since that function only assumes lines concatenate back to whatever string it was handed.

fix(tui): stop the calm preset from selecting the densest transcript

The `calm` preset advertises "a quiet, readable transcript over
debug-dense output", and then set `transcript_spacing = "compact"` —
the densest rhythm there is. At compact an `Activity` boundary spends
zero rows, so a reasoning block, the tool it ran, and the answer that
followed all fused into one wall with nothing separating them. `/config`
compounded it by describing calm_mode as "Quieter chrome and denser
transcript"; nobody reads the word "calm" as denser.

Calm now selects `comfortable`, which is what it always claimed to be,
and the description says what the preset actually does. The spacing
matrix itself is untouched: compact still means "reasoning and its
answer read as one response block" for anyone who deliberately picks it
(crates/tui/src/tui/transcript.rs, and the test of the same name).

Existing installs carry the bad value in settings.toml, so a one-way
migration lifts exactly the stored calm+compact combination once. It is
flag-guarded rather than conditional, so re-choosing compact afterwards
sticks, and a user who chose compact *without* calm is never touched —
that was a real choice.

content.text:
Full CI is now running on my head — the first real verdict on this branch in a while. Here's where things stand.

## Landed, verified, pushed (3 commits)

**1. `76bba1231` — agy sign-in fix (the in-flight work).** Finished it. Two things the handoff claimed were clean were not: `cargo check` failed on a dead `refresh_token` field, and clippy failed on `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations`. A backgrounded clippy even reported **exit 0 with empty output** while the foreground run of the identical command failed — so that's a third false-green this cycle. I dropped the refresh token from the type entirely rather than `#[allow]`-ing it, which also makes the read-only contract structural: the value can't leak because there's no field to leak it from. Added 4 synthetic-envelope tests (no real token material). `16 passed` on the slice, `11188 passed; 0 failed` full suite.

**2. `a1e6e5386` — your spacing complaint.** Root-caused, and it's a real defect. Your `~/.codewhale/settings.toml` has `transcript_spacing = "compact"`, which you never chose — the `calm` preset wrote it. At compact, an `Activity` boundary spends **zero** rows, so reasoning → the tool it ran → the answer all fuse. `/config` even described calm as *"Quieter chrome and denser transcript"*.

I first tried making compact always breathe around answers — then found `compact_spacing_keeps_reasoning_and_answer_in_one_response_block`, a test asserting exactly the opposite on purpose. So I **reverted that** and fixed the actual bug instead: calm now selects `comfortable`, the description tells the truth, and a one-way flag-guarded migration lifts the stored calm+compact combination once. Compact still means what it always meant for anyone who picks it deliberately. `11190 passed; 0 failed`.

**3. `09b43038b` — a red CI gate nobody mentioned.** `check-readme-translations.py` is an unconditional CI leg and it has been **failing with 36 errors on every push** since `d070d510c` added `docs/AUTOMATION.md` to the README without touching the 18 translations. Fixed the link in all 18 using each language's own connector, restamped. Both gates now pass.

## Three claims in the handoff that were false

- **#5600 is fabricated.** It's a closed spam issue titled *"How Much Does Behavioral Health Medical Billing Cost in Texas?"* Zero commits anywhere. Nothing was fixed.
- **#5569 is Unix-only.** The hard-link guard is behind `#[cfg(unix)]`; Windows is explicitly unguarded.
- **#5568 is a no-op by default.** `sandbox_denied_read_paths` defaults empty, so out of the box the full-disk read in the issue still happens — but CHANGELOG claims it "bounds full-disk reads in any posture". That's an overclaim worth correcting before release.

## The buried lede — this reframes the release lane

**PR #5606 was merged to main yesterday at 23:52** (`3a50fdca2`). It carried a **rebased copy of 75 of this branch's commits**. Your local `origin/main` was stale, which made `rev-list` report "105 0" — falsely ahead-only. Real divergence: 106 ahead, 78 behind, and 75 of those 78 are duplicates. Only 2 commits on main are genuinely new.

So the instruction "take #5606 once he adds a Closes line" is moot — it's already in.

I probed the reconciliation in a throwaway worktree: **7 conflicted files, 14 hunks** — `CHANGELOG.md`, `crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md`, and the four mega-files I decomposed for #5586 (main has the pre-extraction versions). Not the ~75-file disaster the recon predicted. Tractable in one sitting. I aborted and removed the probe — I haven't merged anything.

## `[Image #1]` — the honest shape

The compact token is only reachable by hiding the path, and the path is the long part. Shortening the stored line gets you `[Image #1: /Users/.../Screenshot 2026-08-24 at 10.31.22.png]` — barely better.

Worth knowing: `sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments` redacts these lines so a managed-chat host never sees a local path, and it shares the parser with four stores that re-parse across restarts (sessions/backtrack, offline queue, composer history, stash). Changing the stored format risks that redaction failing open. The render-only approach has **zero** persistence or security exposure — it never changes stored text — at the cost of a display↔buffer index map through the composer's cursor/selection/mouse math. That's the right trade, and it's what I'll build next.

**Nothing released, tagged, bumped, or merged to main.** `Cargo.toml` is still `0.9.11`. I'll report the CI verdict when it lands, then start the composer work — say the word if you'd rather I take the main reconciliation or PR #5584 (draft, CI-green, `Closes #5543`, the cleanest merge available) first.

export const meta = {
  name: 'v0912-wave2',
  description: 'Design the composer display map, review PR #5584, plan the main reconciliation, audit CHANGELOG accuracy',
  phases: [{ title: 'Investigate' }],
}

const REPO = '/Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/codewhale'

const RULES = `
READ-ONLY investigation in the Codewhale repo at ${REPO}, branch codex/v0912-integration-20260823 (head 09b43038b).

ABSOLUTE RULES:
- Do NOT edit, create, or delete ANY file. No git commits, no writes, no git checkout/stash/reset/merge/rebase.
- THREE other agents are concurrently editing this repo (crates/computer-use/, plugins/, cli/, web/, and a docs worktree). Never run 'cargo fmt --all'. Never touch their files.
- You MAY create a throwaway git worktree under /private/tmp/ if you need to inspect a merge, but you MUST remove it before finishing and MUST NOT leave any merge state behind.
- Verify claims against the code. Prior agents in this lane have made several false claims (a "suite green" that hid a stack overflow, a fabricated issue fix, a background clippy reporting exit 0 while the same command failed in the foreground). Trust nothing you are told; cite file:line.
Your final text IS the return value. Be dense, concrete, and honest about uncertainty.
`

const OUT = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['summary', 'findings', 'recommendation', 'risks'],
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['file', 'line', 'what'],
        properties: {
          file: { type: 'string' },
          line: { type: 'integer' },
          what: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    recommendation: { type: 'string' },
    risks: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

phase('Investigate')

const tasks = [
  {
    label: 'composer-display-map',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: Produce an EXACT implementation plan for rendering composer image attachments as a compact "[Image #N]" token (Claude Code style), WITHOUT changing the stored buffer text.

BACKGROUND (already established — do not re-derive, but DO verify the line numbers still hold):
- The composer buffer 'app.input' stores a whole line per attachment: "[Attached image: 1920x1440 PNG (2.3MB) at /path/shot.png]", produced by media_attachment_reference() in crates/tui/src/tui/app.rs (~line 5865) and parsed back by media_attachment_references() in crates/tui/src/tui/file_mention.rs (~line 757).
- The stored text MUST NOT change: it is re-parsed from four persisted stores (saved sessions via apply_backtrack, sessions/checkpoints/offline_queue.json, ~/.codewhale/composer_history.txt, ~/.codewhale/composer_stash.jsonl), AND the same parser backs sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments (crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs ~line 130), the Runtime-Chat guard that redacts local paths from a managed host. So this is a RENDER-ONLY change.
- There is one existing display-vs-buffer hook: App::composer_display_input() / composer_display_cursor() in crates/tui/src/tui/app/composer.rs (~574/578), but it is a whole-buffer swap for history search returning &str, and mouse hit-testing bypasses it (crates/tui/src/tui/mouse_ui.rs ~174, ~239 read raw app.input).

DELIVER:
1. Verify each file:line above still matches. Correct any that drifted.
2. Enumerate EVERY call site that reads app.input (or composer_display_input) for rendering, cursor placement, selection painting, wrapping, or mouse mapping. For each: file:line, what it does, and what it must become. Look especially at crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs (wrap_input_lines_internal, cursor row/col math ~4062, selection ~1504, cursor_pos ~1826), crates/tui/src/tui/frame.rs (~1093, ~1124), crates/tui/src/tui/mouse_ui.rs (~174, ~239).
3. Propose the concrete type. Something like ComposerDisplay { text: String, display_to_buffer: Vec<usize>, buffer_to_display: Vec<usize> } built once per frame, collapsing each whole attachment LINE to a token. Specify: where it is built, where it is cached/invalidated, and whether char or byte indices (state which the surrounding code uses).
4. Cursor atomicity: which functions must treat a collapsed token as one unit so the caret does not appear frozen while crossing ~60 buffer chars. Name them (move_cursor_left/right, backspace/delete, word motion, home/end, selection extend) with file:line.
5. Numbering: N is positional over media_attachment_references order. Since the number is DISPLAY-only under this design, confirm it can simply be the enumeration index at render time (no buffer rewrite, no stale numbers, no renumber pass). Verify that reasoning.
6. List existing tests that will need updating vs. those that will keep passing untouched (render-only should break far fewer than a format change). Give file:line.
7. Give a STAGED plan: what is the smallest first commit that is independently correct and shippable, and what can follow.

Return the structured object.`,
  },
  {
    label: 'pr5584-review',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: Review PR #5584 ("fix(subagents): persist child approval receipts", author cyq1017, branch codex/codewhale-5543-child-approval-receipts, currently DRAFT, MERGEABLE/CLEAN, body says "Closes #5543"). This is a P0 safety item. Decide whether it is correct enough to take.

Use gh: 'gh pr view 5584', 'gh pr diff 5584', 'gh pr checks 5584', and 'gh issue view 5543' for the requirement.

Established context to verify, not assume: #5543 is NOT implemented on the integration branch. ApprovalReceipt / ApprovalReceiptStore / ApprovalReplay exist in crates/tui/src/approval_log.rs and are wired at crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs (~893-910, 1101, 1125) for the PARENT session path only. grep 'ApprovalReceipt' under crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/ reportedly returns zero hits on the branch.

DELIVER:
1. Confirm or correct the above (does the child path really not exist on the branch?).
2. Read the full PR diff. Summarize precisely what it changes, file by file.
3. Correctness review, focused on what actually matters for an approval-receipt path:
   - Does a child's approval genuinely persist and replay, or only within one process?
   - Can a child inherit or forge an approval it was not granted? Is the receipt scoped to the child that earned it?
   - Any way a denial is lost, or an approval outlives the scope it was granted for?
   - Concurrency: two children approving at once; a child dying mid-approval.
   - Does it reuse the existing approval_log.rs spine, or add a parallel one? AGENTS.md forbids adding a second legacy call site / parallel system.
4. Does it respect the single-turn-loop invariant (Engine::run_turn) and add no second loop?
5. Does its CHANGELOG receipt exist and cite #5543? Check the PR diff for a CHANGELOG hunk.
6. Report the exact CI leg results from 'gh pr checks 5584'.
7. Verdict: TAKE AS-IS / TAKE WITH SPECIFIC FIXES (list them) / DO NOT TAKE (why).

Return the structured object.`,
  },
  {
    label: 'main-reconciliation',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: Produce a per-file resolution plan for merging origin/main into the integration branch.

ESTABLISHED (verify, do not assume): origin/main is now 3a50fdca2 (merge of PR #5606, merged 2026-08-24T23:52). It contains a REBASED COPY of 75 of this branch's commits under different SHAs. 'git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main' = 106/78. Only 2 commits on main are genuinely new:
  - fix(shell): accept Windows verbatim-path operands; changelog receipt for C3
  - fix(test): keep the mock-client host-managed engine test through the rebase

A probe merge (git merge origin/main --no-commit --no-ff) produced exactly 7 conflicted files / 14 conflict hunks:
  CHANGELOG.md (3), crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md (3), crates/tui/src/client.rs (1), crates/tui/src/config.rs (1), crates/tui/src/lib.rs (2), crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs (2), crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/tests.rs (2)

Context that explains most of them: this branch performed 9 mechanical "#5586" extractions that decomposed the mega-files (lib.rs 18.7k->13.1k, config.rs, client.rs, runtime_threads.rs) into submodules. Main has the PRE-extraction versions (rebased). So the branch side is the newer architecture and generally wins, but main's 2 genuinely-new commits must not be lost.

DELIVER:
1. Re-run the probe yourself in a THROWAWAY worktree under /private/tmp/ (e.g. 'git worktree add --detach /private/tmp/recon-merge HEAD', then 'git merge origin/main --no-commit --no-ff'). Confirm the 7 files / 14 hunks. REMOVE the worktree when done (git merge --abort; git worktree remove --force).
2. For EACH of the 7 files, show the actual conflict hunks and state the correct resolution: take branch side, take main side, or hand-merge (and exactly how). Be specific about content, not generic advice.
3. CRITICAL: determine where main's 2 genuinely-new commits land. Does 'fix(shell): accept Windows verbatim-path operands' survive the merge, or is it inside a conflict hunk where taking the branch side would silently DROP it? Same for the mock-client test fix. Name the files/functions they touch.
4. Check whether the branch already has an equivalent of those 2 fixes under a different commit (the branch reportedly did #5595 Windows work). If the branch has its own version, say which is better and why.
5. State whether crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md should be hand-resolved at all, or regenerated with scripts/sync-changelog.sh after resolving the root CHANGELOG.md. Read that script to be sure.
6. Give the exact command sequence for the reconciliation, and the verification commands that must pass afterwards.

Return the structured object.`,
  },
  {
    label: 'changelog-accuracy',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: Audit the [Unreleased] section of ${REPO}/CHANGELOG.md for CLAIMS THAT OVERSTATE WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES. This ships as release notes, so an overclaim is a correctness bug.

Note: CHANGELOG.md is dirty in the working tree — another agent added an uncommitted ~17-line 'computer-use' block at the top of ### Added. Read the working-tree version, but clearly separate committed entries from that uncommitted block.

TWO OVERCLAIMS ARE ALREADY KNOWN — verify them and find the rest:
(a) #5568 sandbox read deny-list: CHANGELOG reportedly says it 'bounds full-disk reads in any posture', but the config field sandbox_denied_read_paths defaults to EMPTY, so out of the box the full-disk read described in issue #5568 still happens. Verify in crates/tui/src/config.rs and crates/tui/src/sandbox/{seatbelt,bwrap}.rs.
(b) #5569 hard-link write escape: the guard in crates/tui/src/utils.rs (~288) is behind #[cfg(unix)] and Windows is explicitly unguarded, but the CHANGELOG may not say so. Verify.

DELIVER:
1. For EVERY entry in [Unreleased] that cites an issue number, spot-check the claim against the implementing code. Focus on entries claiming safety, security, money/cost, or data-integrity properties — those are where an overclaim actually hurts.
2. Report each overclaim as: the exact CHANGELOG sentence, what the code actually does (file:line), and a corrected sentence that is accurate and no longer than the original.
3. Flag any entry citing an issue with NO implementation on the branch at all (a phantom receipt). In particular check #5543 — it should NOT have a receipt, because the implementation lives in unmerged draft PR #5584.
4. Report the uncommitted computer-use block: it reportedly cites no issue number at all. Confirm, and note whether scripts/release/check-feature-release-notes.sh would care (read the script — it only gates commits whose SUBJECT matches ^feat:).
5. Do NOT propose rewriting entries that are accurate. Only report real defects. If an entry is fine, say nothing about it.

Return the structured object. Put the exact corrected sentences in 'recommendation'.`,
  },
]

const results = await parallel(
  tasks.map((t) => () =>
    agent(t.prompt, { label: t.label, phase: 'Investigate', schema: OUT })
      .then((r) => ({ area: t.label, ...r }))
  )
)

return { results: results.filter(Boolean) }

docs(changelog): correct three more overstated 0.9.12 claims

Follow-up to the #5568/#5569 corrections. Each of these was verified
against the implementing code, not the commit message.

#5567 claimed a "cost/token usage ceiling" that bounds "a whole run's
spend". `FleetUsageCeiling` (crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs:846) carries
exactly one field, `max_total_tokens`. There is no currency denomination
anywhere in the type, so the ceiling cannot bound spend — a run of
expensive models and a run of cheap ones hit it at the same token count.
Say tokens, and say plainly that a cost ceiling is not shipped.

#5578 credited this release with the footer showing `cost: unknown` when
nothing can be priced. That text is already present in v0.9.11
(route_billing.rs, provider_picker.rs, sidebar.rs), and the #5578 commit
(48453b744) touches only app.rs, app/tests.rs and ui/event_loop.rs. The
per-step pricing is genuinely new; the footer is not.

#5588 named only one leak direction, and it is the less consequential
one. Commit b88462574 removed `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` from NVIDIA NIM's
credential fallback list, which had been silently sending a DeepSeek key
to NVIDIA's endpoint on provider switch. A reader deciding what to
rotate needed that direction stated, so it is now named explicitly.

Two further citations look questionable but are left alone rather than
guessed at: the trailing "(#5528)" on the responseSchema bullet has no
implementing commit, and #5528 also covers dispatch errors while the
shipped work covers schema errors.

Evidence:

  git show 48453b744 --stat              (footer files untouched)
  git grep "cost: unknown" v0.9.11       (predates this release)
  git show b88462574                     (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY removed from NIM)
  bash scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check -> up to date

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

SUMMARY:
 PR #5584 (cyq1017, branch codex/codewhale-5543-child-approval-receipts, head 2d220733c, DRAFT, MERGEABLE/CLEAN, +343/-11 across 3 files) is a correct, tightly-scoped fix for #5543 that I verified against the code rather than the PR body.

BASELINE CONFIRMED. `grep -rn 'ApprovalReceipt' /Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/codewhale/crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/` returns exit 1 / zero hits on 09b43038b. The receipt spine exists only in the parent path: `crates/tui/src/approval_log.rs` (ApprovalReceipt 26, ApprovalReceiptStore 153, ApprovalReplay 82, append 259, replay 253), `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:893/897/908`, `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:751/1516/1551`, `crates/tui/src/core/engine/approval.rs:57-120`. The child path did not exist. Confirmed as stated.

WHAT IT CHANGES, FILE BY FILE.
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs` (+2/-0): adds `.with_approval_receipt_store(self.approval_receipt_store.clone())` to both SubAgentRuntime builders — the per-turn one at ~4108 and the off-turn `off_turn_subagent_runtime` one at ~5460.
- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs` (+145/-9): new private field `approval_receipt_store: Option<Result<ApprovalReceiptStore, String>>` on `SubAgentRuntime` (2467), `None` in `new()` (2527), `pub(crate) with_approval_receipt_store` builder (2554), propagated in `child_runtime()` (2863); new `SubAgentToolRegistry::commit_child_approval_receipt` (~14409) mirroring `Engine::commit_approval_receipt`; `prompt_parent_for_child_call` now commits `Asked` immediately after `register_child_approval` and BEFORE the `Event::ApprovalRequired` send (~14491), commits `Decided(Unavailable)` when the send fails (~14530), replaces the `Option<ChildApprovalOutcome>` wait result with a 3-variant `WaitOutcome{Answer,Cancelled,Unavailable}` so a dropped oneshot is no longer mislabelled as user cancellation, and commits the terminal `ApprovedOnce|Denied|Cancelled|Unavailable` before returning any verdict — a failed terminal commit returns `Deny`, never `Proceed`.
- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/tests.rs` (+196/-2): `stub_runtime()` field init; test harness now installs a real `ApprovalReceiptStore` on a tempdir and a unique `state_namespace`; 4 new tests (`ask_without_a_durable_receipt_store_fails_closed_before_prompting`, `closed_child_approval_waiter_persists_unavailable_not_cancelled`, `cancelled_child_approval_persists_cancelled`, `unavailable_prompt_host_persists_unavailable`, `terminal_receipt_failure_blocks_an_approved_child_call`) plus assertions that the `Asked` is on disk before the human answers and that an approved-but-uncommitted call does not touch the filesystem.

CORRECTNESS.
- Genuinely durable, not process-local. `gate_runtime.context.state_namespace` is the parent SESSION ID: the only production setter of `state_namespace` in the whole workspace is `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:5678 .with_state_namespace(self.session.id.clone())` in `build_tool_context_for_turn`, and `child_runtime()` clones that context (mod.rs:2936). So child receip

=== RECOMMENDATION ===
 TAKE WITH SPECIFIC FIXES.

The safety substance is correct and I could not find a way to defeat it: `Asked` is committed before the prompt is exposed, every terminal outcome is committed before the gate closes, a failed commit returns `Deny` and never `Proceed`, denial survives a commit failure, receipts land in the parent session's real durable log (not a per-process store), a child can only receive the decision for its own approval id, and the previously conflated "cancelled vs. channel closed" case is now distinguished. It reuses approval_log.rs rather than forking a second receipt system, adds no second turn loop, and both production runtimes that can prompt are wired. The patch applies cleanly to 09b43038b (verified plain and 3-way in a throwaway worktree, since removed) and the real CI legs (macOS 33m, Windows 19m) are green with all 13 child_permission_gate tests, including the 4 new ones, executed by name.

Required before merge:
1. Add the CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased] / ### Fixed` entry citing #5543 and crediting cyq1017. This is the only true blocker and is a one-line fix.
2. Mark the PR ready for review (it is still DRAFT).

Strongly recommended, cheap, and safe to do in the same PR:
3. Collapse `commit_child_approval_receipt` (subagent/mod.rs ~14409) and `Engine::commit_approval_receipt` (core/engine/approval.rs:57) onto one shared helper in approval_log.rs so the fail-closed contract cannot drift.
4. Mix the per-process boot id or a fresh uuid into the child approval id at mod.rs:3447 to eliminate the resume-collision denial.

Acceptable to defer to follow-up issues:
5. Structured agent_id / real tool-call-id on child receipts (finding 3).
6. Durable receipts for guardian-approved child calls (finding 5) and an actual consumer for `replay_approvals` (finding 6).

If you need this landed today and cannot wait on the author, taking it with only fix 1 applied is defensible — findings 2-6 are quality and completeness, not correctness of the fail-closed path.

collapses each attachment line to `[Image #N]` (or `[Video #N]`) and
carries the mapping back to buffer coordinates, so the text, the caret,

  the display borrows the buffer and allocates nothing, which is the
  overwhelmingly common frame.

- The caret crosses a collapsed line in one step. Stepping through it
  grapheme by grapheme would look like a frozen cursor for the ~60
  characters the token hides.

  highlights the whole token rather than a fraction of it.

content.text:
All other agents' work intact; everything of mine is committed and pushed. Fresh CI is running on the new head.

## This session's landed work (9 commits, all pushed, all verified)

**Your two asks:**

- **Spacing** — `a1e6e5386`. Root cause was the `calm` preset writing `transcript_spacing = "compact"`, which spends **zero** rows at `Activity` boundaries, fusing reasoning → tool → answer. I first tried making compact always breathe, then found `compact_spacing_keeps_reasoning_and_answer_in_one_response_block` asserting the opposite *on purpose* — so I reverted that and fixed the actual trap instead. Calm now selects `comfortable`, `/config` no longer advertises it as "denser transcript", and a one-way migration lifts your stored calm+compact once.

- **`[Image #1]`** — `81a1afdac`. Render-only, which turned out to be the *safer* option, not just the prettier one: `sanitize_isolated_chat_attachments` parses that same attachment line to strip local paths before anything reaches a managed Runtime Chat host, and four persisted stores re-parse it across restarts. Changing the stored format risks that redaction failing open on text restored from an older store. So the buffer is untouched and only the paint changes. Caret crosses a token in one step; selection edges floor/ceil so a token highlights whole.

**CI was red and nobody knew** — the test legs had never run on this head. I dispatched a full run and got three real failures:

- **Documentation** (`747cadd26`) — 3 broken intra-doc links failed `cargo doc -Dwarnings`. This leg only runs on `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch`, so no PR run has *ever* executed it.
- **Test (windows)** (`6dc3d093d`) — a test fed 2 MiB of `0xFF` and demanded U+FFFD. Windows decodes via the ANSI code page after #5602, where `0xFF` is a valid `ÿ`. The assertion was demanding exactly the mojibake #5602 removed.
- **Safety gate** — **a genuine flake**, not a regression. I reproduced it locally twice in ~35 runs of the same filter. `RuntimeChatRelayHost::open` fails intermittently under parallel load. Same class as #5605. I have not fixed it — I'd be guessing at the mechanism, and I'd rather tell you that than ship a speculative fix.

**Contributor work:** `93e0ffd24` closes the new issue **#5607** from @diegovskytl — OpenCode Go is a gateway whose roster is whatever the key unlocks, but the catalog refresh was gated on a hard-coded pair of providers. All the plumbing already existed. I replaced the `matches!` with a named rule so the next gateway doesn't get forgotten.

**Release-note accuracy** (`1efd9c79e`, `de6a29f18`) — five overstated claims corrected. The one that mattered: #5588 said "NVIDIA credentials no longer leak into the DeepSeek keychain" but the actual fix removed `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` from NVIDIA NIM's fallback list — a **DeepSeek** key was being sent to NVIDIA. The note told readers to rotate the wrong key. content.text: Now it's clearly a bug, not just clutter: the footer advertises **`a-z` jump**, but `s` was stolen — so typing `s` couldn't jump to SenseNova, Siliconflow, Stepfun, or SGLang. Let me fix it.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='crates/tui/src/tui/provider_picker.rs'
s=open(p).read()

# 1. Drop the dedicated action-bar button (both footers).
before = s.count('                    ActionHint::new("S", "SenseNova"),\n')
assert before == 2, before
s = s.replace('                    ActionHint::new("S", "SenseNova"),\n', '')

# 2. Drop the dedicated key handler; `s` returns to the a-z jump the footer advertises.
handler = '''                KeyCode::Char(c)
                    if key.modifiers.is_empty()
                        && self.query.is_empty()
                        && c.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&'s') =>
                {
                    self.enter_sensenova_form();
                    ViewAction::None
                }
'''
assert handler in s
s = s.replace(handler, '', 1)

# 3. The form entry had exactly one caller.
form = '''    fn enter_sensenova_form(&mut self) {
        if let Some(template) = provider_setup_template(SENSENOVA_TEMPLATE_ID) {
            self.apply_template(template);
        }
    }

'''
assert form in s
s = s.replace(form, '', 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("button, key handler, and form entry removed")
PY

export const meta = {
  name: 'v0912-model-taxonomy',
  description: 'Audit model categorization correctness and design a richer provider screen',
  phases: [{ title: 'Audit' }],
}

const REPO = '/Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/codewhale'

const RULES = `
READ-ONLY investigation in the Codewhale repo at ${REPO}, branch codex/v0912-integration-20260823.

ABSOLUTE RULES:
- Do NOT edit, create, or delete ANY file. No git writes. No cargo fmt --all. Read/grep only.
- THREE other agents are concurrently editing this repo (crates/computer-use/, plugins/, cli/, web/). Never touch their files.
- Cite file:line for every claim. Say "uncertain" rather than guessing.
- The user's exact words: "some of our model categorization is sketchy" and they want the provider screen to "show something like what fleet roles exist for certain models, or trying to fill it in with more information, or organizing it differently by using artificial analysis".
Your final text IS the return value. Be dense and concrete. Prioritise DEFECTS over inventory.
`

const OUT = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['summary', 'findings', 'recommendation', 'risks'],
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['file', 'line', 'what'],
        properties: {
          file: { type: 'string' },
          line: { type: 'integer' },
          what: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    recommendation: { type: 'string' },
    risks: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

phase('Audit')

const tasks = [
  {
    label: 'model-facts-audit',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: Find CONCRETE ERRORS in Codewhale's hard-coded model facts. The user says the categorization is "sketchy" — your job is to produce a list of specific wrong entries, not a tour.

WHERE TO LOOK (verify these paths exist, correct any drift):
- crates/tui/src/models.rs — context_window_for_model() and friends; lots of hard-coded per-model numbers with comments citing dates.
- crates/tui/src/model_registry.rs
- crates/tui/src/model_profile.rs
- crates/tui/src/pricing.rs — per-model pricing / billing surfaces.
- crates/config/src/provider_templates.rs — per-provider default_model and models lists.
- crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs and crates/tui/src/provider_lake.rs — the live Models.dev catalog that is supposed to override the bundled numbers.

DELIVER:
1. The full inventory of DIMENSIONS along which a model is categorized (context window, vision/modality, tool-call support, reasoning support, tier/class, pricing, default-ness, aliases). For each: where it is stored, and whether it is bundled-static, live-fetched, or both.
2. THE MAIN DELIVERABLE — a list of specific entries that look WRONG or STALE. Look hard for:
   - Models whose bundled context window contradicts the comment above it, or contradicts the same model's entry elsewhere in the repo.
   - The SAME model appearing under two providers with DIFFERENT facts (context window, pricing, capability). This is the highest-value class of bug — report every instance you find.
   - Capability flags asserted for a model family rather than a model (e.g. all of provider X marked vision-capable because one model is).
   - Alias tables mapping a slug to the wrong canonical model.
   - Comments citing a date (e.g. "as of 2026-08-08") that are now stale relative to the repo's current date of 2026-08-25, especially where a newer model exists in the same table.
   - Defaults pointing at a model the provider does not actually serve (there is precedent: the openai provider once defaulted to deepseek-v4-pro).
3. Where the bundled value and the live Models.dev value disagree, state which one wins at runtime and whether the bundled one can ever shadow a correct live one.
4. Rank your findings by user-visible harm: a wrong context window causes premature or missed compaction; wrong pricing causes wrong cost display; a wrong capability flag causes a hard request failure.

Return the structured object. Put the ranked defect list in 'findings' and the fix order in 'recommendation'.`,
  },
  {
    label: 'fleet-roles-in-picker',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: The user wants the provider/model screen to surface WHAT A MODEL IS FOR — specifically "what fleet roles exist for certain models". Work out what data already exists to support that, and design the smallest honest version.

INVESTIGATE:
1. What IS a fleet role in this codebase? Find the role taxonomy. Look at crates/tui/src/fleet/, crates/protocol/src/fleet.rs, and anything about "role posture" (issue #5575 says role posture has no single source of truth — find out whether that is still true and where the candidate sources are).
2. Is there any existing mapping from a model (or model capability) to a role, or a recommended-model-per-role? Or is role assignment purely user-configured? Be precise — this determines whether the feature is "surface existing data" or "invent new data".
3. Where would it render? Read crates/tui/src/tui/provider_picker.rs (~8400 lines): find the row-rendering function, the detail/side panel for a selected provider, and what per-model info is shown TODAY when a user browses models (there is a models stage — find it, look for MessageId::PickerActionModels).
4. Assess the "Artificial Analysis" idea. Codewhale already integrates models.dev via crates/tui/src/models_dev_live.rs with a disk cache and background refresh. Report how that integration works (fetch, cache path, refresh cadence, failure behavior, and crucially its KV-cache/offline implications per docs/CACHE.md and the AGENTS.md offline rule). Then say whether an Artificial Analysis-style quality/speed/price index could ride the SAME mechanism, and what it would cost. Flag honestly if adding a second external data source conflicts with the project's offline-first and footprint goals — the standing product goal is "fast, slim, easy to run".
5. Propose the SMALLEST change that makes the model list genuinely more informative using data Codewhale ALREADY has locally (no new network dependency). Be concrete about which fields and which render site.

Return the structured object.`,
  },
  {
    label: 'provider-screen-neutrality',
    prompt: `${RULES}

TASK: The user just had a per-provider hotkey removed from the provider picker (a dedicated "S = SenseNova" button that stole a letter from the advertised a-z jump). Find the REST of the arbitrary per-provider special-casing in the provider/model UI, so we can judge what else should go.

INVESTIGATE crates/tui/src/tui/provider_picker.rs (~8400 lines) and crates/tui/src/tui/views/:
1. Enumerate EVERY place the picker branches on a specific ApiProvider variant or a specific template id. For each, classify it as:
   (a) LEGITIMATE — encodes a real protocol/auth difference the provider actually has (e.g. an OAuth-only route, a provider that needs a billing-route choice, a compatibility shim).
   (b) ARBITRARY — a convenience shortcut, a hand-picked ordering, or a hard-coded label that any provider could equally claim.
   Give file:line and a one-line justification for the classification. Be rigorous: do not call something arbitrary just because it names a provider.
2. Specifically list the remaining top-level single-letter hotkeys in the picker's key handler and which are provider-specific vs categorical. Note which ones collide with the a-z type-ahead jump the footer advertises.
3. Look at the action-bar footers (search ActionHint::new) and report whether the hint set is getting overcrowded — count the hints in each footer variant.
4. Report the provider ORDERING logic: is the row order alphabetical, hand-curated, or tiered? If hand-curated, where is the list and does it privilege particular providers without stating why?
5. Cross-check against issue #5588 (provider neutrality: DeepSeek-exclusive gates). Report which of the gates you found overlap with what #5588 already tracks, so we do not double-file.

Return the structured object. Put the (a)/(b) classified list in 'findings' and a recommended removal order in 'recommendation'.`,
  },
]

const results = await parallel(
  tasks.map((t) => () =>
    agent(t.prompt, { label: t.label, phase: 'Audit', schema: OUT })
      .then((r) => ({ area: t.label, ...r }))
  )
)

return { results: results.filter(Boolean) }

SenseNova's gone. Here's where things stand while the categorization audit runs.

## The SenseNova button — it wasn't just clutter

You were right that there's no reason for it, and it turned out to be an actual bug rather than a cosmetic one.

`S` had a dedicated key handler *and* its own `ActionHint` button in both footer variants. It's one of four compatible templates — `opencode-zen`, `opencode-go`, `sensenova`, `agnes` — and the only one with a button. `P` already opens the list containing all of them.

The real problem: the wide footer advertises **`a-z` jump**, and the `S` arm sat ahead of the type-ahead arm with the same guard the `A` handler documents. So typing `s` couldn't jump to SenseNova, SiliconFlow, Stepfun, or SGLang. One provider's shortcut broke the advertised behavior for every provider starting with that letter. Removing it hands the letter back.

I also found `ProviderCustomFormHint` literally said *"SenseNova: S"* — now false. That string lives in 15 locales, and locale **parity** would have stayed green the whole time because the keys never changed, only the meaning. So I fixed the text in all 14 translations too rather than leaving it wrong in every language but English.

The keyboard test that existed only to pin `S` is rewritten to walk the template list, so it now covers the path every other template uses and keeps its "a preset must not render as a blank custom form" assertion. `90d878442`, 11204 passed / 0 failed.

## CI is fully green

The run on `47ceab9bb` — the head including the PR #5584 merge — came back **success on every leg**. That closes out all three failures I found earlier: Documentation and Windows fixed, Safety gate confirmed as a flake.

## On your two new points

**"Some of our model categorization is sketchy"** — audit running now. The class of bug I most expect to find is the same model carrying *different* facts under two providers (context window, pricing, capability), since those tables are hand-maintained per provider. A wrong context window causes premature or missed compaction, so it's worth being exact about.

**Fleet roles / Artificial Analysis in the provider screen** — I want to flag one thing before anyone builds it. Codewhale already pulls models.dev via `models_dev_live.rs` with a disk cache and background refresh, so the *mechanism* exists and a quality/speed/price index could ride it. But adding a second external data source cuts against the standing "fast, slim, easy to run" goal and the offline rule, so I've asked for an honest cost read alongside a version built only from data we already hold locally. I'd rather show you both and let you pick than quietly add a network dependency to the startup path.

I'll report the audit findings when they land, then pick up the main reconciliation (7 files / 14 hunks) unless you want something else first.
